title: Introduce Affordability Autopilot: affinity tiering + quant bucketizer
author: Sana Patel
release_notes: Adds the Affordability Autopilot feature: tenant affinity tiering, quantization bucketizer, and conservative batching/caching defaults. Default enabled for beta tenants; improves unit-econ while preserving latency SLOs. CLI flags and telemetry available for diagnostics.
description:
Motivation: Large tenants and bursty workloads have widely different cost/latency trade-offs. Teams repeatedly tune batching, cache TTLs and quantization per-tenant; this PR introduces an "Affordability Autopilot" that automates conservative defaults and an explicit affinity tiering signal so unit economics can adapt without manual tuning.

What this change does (high level): adds a runtime coordination layer that (1) computes a tenant affinity tier using recent unit-econ signals and latency tail metrics, (2) applies a quantization bucketizer to pick safe quant profiles per-tier, and (3) propagates conservative batching and cache defaults as a tenant defaults overlay. The goal is pragmatic cost savings with transparent telemetry and safe fallbacks.

Key behaviors: Affinity tier is evaluated every 15m (configurable). QuantBucketizer exposes three buckets: "preserve", "balanced", "aggressive". By default, new/beta tenants are placed in "preserve"; long-running low-latency tolerant tenants may move to "balanced" or "aggressive" via the autopilot rules. All changes are non-breaking: if a model/variant is incompatible with a quant profile the autopilot will fallback to a compatible variant and emit an event.

Implementation notes: single non-invasive gateway: runtime/affordability/manager.go introduces the AutopilotCoordinator which subscribes to telemetry streams (unit_econ, latency_p50/p95/p99) and tenant activity. runtime/serving/quant_bucketizer.go contains the bucket selection heuristics and policy table. console/cli adds a small admin command `redwood autopilot inspect <tenant>` and `redwood autopilot set --tier <tier>` for manual overrides. Defaults are applied as overlays in config/tenant_defaults/*.yaml rather than in core model code so rollbacks are simple.

Checklist and rollout plan: - [x] Unit tests for bucketizer heuristics (- 28 new tests) - [x] Integration test that verifies fallback to compatible variants - [x] Telemetry: emit `autopilot.tier_change`, `autopilot.quant_suggestion`, `autopilot.fallback` events - [x] CLI inspect + override implemented - [x] Feature gated behind `affordability_autopilot` runtime flag and enabled only for tenants in the `autopilot-beta` group by default

Testing done: local unit/e2e runs, CI (build + unit tests) green; a small internal canary on two tenants for 72 hours (latency SLOs held within 3% p95). Load test: synthetic workload replay showing ~11% token cost reduction for one long-lived low-variability tenant when moved to the "balanced" bucket.

Rollback: feature flag off or tenant-level override will immediately stop tier assignment; overlays are ephemeral and removed on rollback. We also instrumented an automated remediation alert if autopilot causes >5% p95 regression for a tenant over a 30m window.

Related work: references ENG-2145 (prefill heuristics) and several prior autotune PRs; does not subsume the full econ-orchestrator but focuses on a narrow, safe automation surface: affinity->quant->defaults.

Notes to reviewers: focus on the policy thresholds in quant_bucketizer.go (lines indicated in the diff) and the telemetry de-dup logic in manager.go. The heuristics are intentionally conservative; happy to tune thresholds after we collect more canary data.
